honesty.access: anonymous only; no credential is entered, stored, or synthesized, so no premium payload can enter these artifacts
honesty.authority: this harness measures and screenshots; it scores, ranks, and judges nothing
honesty.capture_method: NOT a live `/stocks/MSFT.html` site route capture (this PR is stacked on unmerged #6831 and has never been rendered by the real build pipeline into `site/`). Instead: the real `engine.security_state.compile_security_state_failure` (owner_read_completed=False, the M1 shell) and the real committed golden MSFT fixture (`tests/fixtures/security_state/golden_msft_expected_output.json`) were each passed through the real `scripts.build_ticker_pages.build_security_state()` projection and rendered through the real `templates/ticker.html.j2` (Jinja, `ChainableUndefined` for the page vars this isolated capture does not supply — identical to how `tests/test_security_state_view_model.py` renders this same template). The rendered page's `#security-state` panel's own `<section class="dpanel">` "Identity checks" block (the identity-checks section named in the round-3 review) was extracted with BeautifulSoup, together with the template's own inline <style> block and `templates/theme.css`, into a standalone harness page with no other page chrome (nav, other panels, the `.dsr-dlg` drawer's open/close JS) — same method the PR body described for round-3, now actually captured as committed files rather than only described in prose. Both the golden-MSFT panel (disclosures line only, identity PROVEN, no refusals) and the M1-shell panel (both the refusals AND disclosures `.dfoot .c`-chip lines) are stacked on one harness page so a single capture proves both new lines.
honesty.gaps: states that were not captured are recorded with a reason; nothing is inferred for them
honesty.light_theme_judgment: Judged as a design, not a token swap: light renders a white/near-white cool canvas (`--bg`/`--card` light tokens already defined in `templates/theme.css` for this page's other components), hairline `1px` dividers between R1..R9 receipts, and dark ink text — a materially different surface from dark's luminance-depth panel, per `research/MASTER_PRODUCT_DESIGN_SYSTEM_V1.md`'s dark=command-center / light=research-workspace split. This round's diff adds ONE CSS rule (`.dfoot .c{margin-left:6px;color:var(--muted)}`) and does not introduce a new component, so no NEW light-specific art direction is owed beyond what commit `16c6342b73be` (this panel's original ship, #6831) already established for both themes — this evidence proves that existing dual-theme design still holds with the new chip spacing rule applied, in both themes.
